chapters.title: Workflows: Events, Tasks and Outcomes
chapters.subtitle: What starts a workflow, what it does, and where it goes next

steps.text: A workflow runs because something happens, does its work in tasks, and moves from one activity to the next through outcomes. In this video, you build a workflow that reacts to a published page, and learn what each of these building blocks does.

A workflow is a set of activities connected to each other. An event is an activity that waits for something to happen. As the start activity, it starts the workflow; anywhere else, it makes the workflow wait.
A task is an activity that does something, such as showing a notification, writing to the log, or sending an email. The workflow runs a task when it reaches it.
An outcome tells the workflow how an activity ended, such as Done. Some activities offer several outcomes: an If Else Task has True and False, and an Email Task has Done and Failed.
You connect an outcome to the next activity, and the connection tells the workflow what to run next. An activity that no connection reaches from the start never runs.
Workflows are under Design in the admin menu. Let's open Workflows, where the list is empty, and select Create Workflow.
A workflow only needs a name. Let's type Announce published pages, and select Create and open the designer.
The designer opens on an empty canvas. A workflow runs when something happens, so it offers events to start with. Let's pick Content Published Event.
The event appears on the canvas with a Start badge, because the first event you add becomes the start activity. Its settings open at the bottom.
Content Types filters the event. Let's select Page, so that only publishing a page starts this workflow.

chapters.title: Outcomes and connections
chapters.subtitle: How a workflow moves from one activity to the next

steps.text: The event has one outcome, Done, shown as a port on the right edge of the activity. Pointing at a port that leads nowhere shows a plus. Let's click it.
A menu lists the activities you can add next, and you can search it. Let's search for fork, and select Fork Task.
The Fork Task is added to the right, already connected. The line between the two activities is a connection: when the event finishes with Done, the workflow goes on to the Fork Task.
Some activities have fixed outcomes, but a Fork Task takes its outcomes from its settings. In Forks, you enter names separated by commas. Let's enter Editors, Audit.
The Fork Task shows two outcomes, Editors and Audit. When it runs, the workflow follows both of them, so each outcome can lead somewhere different.
Let's click the Editors outcome, search for notify, and select Notify Task. A task is where the work of the workflow happens.
Notify Task has a Notification Type and a Message. Let's keep Success, and type: Announced by the workflow, a page was published. The activity on the canvas shows the message.
For the Audit outcome, let's use the Activities pane on the left. Search for log, select Tasks to keep only tasks, and click Log.
Log Task writes a line to the log of the site. Let's keep the Information level, and type: Audit, a page was published.
A badge on the Log Task counts its issues. This one is a warning: nothing connects the task to the start activity, so it never runs.
Let's drag from the Audit outcome onto Log Task. The connection is drawn, and the badge disappears.
Notify Task and Log Task each have one outcome, Done. Nothing is connected to it, so each branch ends there, and the workflow finishes once both have run.
The designer saves your changes to a draft, and a draft does not run. Select Publish to make the workflow run. The version shown in the toolbar changes to the one you published.
Let's publish a page. Under Content, Content Items, the New menu lists the content types you can create. Let's choose Page.
Let's type Opening hours as the title, and select Publish. Publishing a page is the event that starts this workflow.
The list comes back with the notification of the Notify Task, next to the message that the page was published.
To check what ran, let's open Instances from the Workflows page. Each run of a workflow is an instance, and this one is Finished.
Let's open the instance. The canvas highlights the activities and connections that ran: the event, the Fork Task, and both branches. A separate video covers instances in detail.
An event starts a workflow or makes it wait, tasks do the work, and outcomes connect one activity to the next. Thanks for watching.
